pageCache.text:
Working in Partnership with Parents
At Our Lady & St Joseph's Catholic Primary School, we recognise that parents and carers are the first and most important educators of their children. We are committed to building strong partnerships between home and school to support every child's personal development, wellbeing and success.
Throughout the year, parents are invited into school to participate in a range of Stay and Play sessions, classroom experiences and school events, providing valuable opportunities to engage with their child's learning and celebrate their achievements. In addition, we offer a variety of parent workshops designed to share practical strategies, approaches and resources that can be used to support learning and development at home.
These sessions aim to strengthen the partnership between families and school, build confidence in supporting children academically and emotionally, and provide parents with valuable tools to help their children thrive. By working together, we can ensure that every child is nurtured, encouraged and supported to reach their full potential with Christ at the centre of all we do.

pageCache.text:
Breakfast Club
Free Universal Breakfast Club
Our Lady & St Joseph Catholic Primary School is delighted to offer a Free Universal Breakfast Club as part of the Department for Education’s Free Breakfast Clubs programme.
The club is open to every pupil from Reception to Year 6, with no charge to parents or carers. It provides children with breakfast and a calm, welcoming start to the school day.
The Department for Education’s programme aims to ensure that all primary-aged children can access a free breakfast club before school.
When does it run?
Our Free Universal Breakfast Club starts at 8:30am each school day, and children can enjoy the Daily Mile with Mr Cuming and Mrs Mensah or enjoy bagels with Ms Webber in the outdoor classroom.
Children can settle into the day before going to class ready to learn.
Who can attend?
The Free Universal Breakfast Club is available to all pupils in Reception to Year 6.
There is no means test, eligibility check or payment required. The programme is designed to be universal, so every child at the school is welcome to attend.
Early Birds Breakfast Club
Our Lady & St Joseph Catholic Primary School provides Breakfast Club provision for up to 40 children (Y1 – Y6) and up to 24 children (EYFS).
The club operates on school premises in a safe environment and run by a team of high-quality trained staff whose purpose is to make sure the children have the very best start to their day.
Drop off Procedure
Breakfast Club starts at 7:30am and the latest time for admission is 8:30am.
Payment Terms
Breakfast club is £3.50 per session. We recommend that payment is made a minimum of 2 days in advance and a credit balance is maintained at all times.
You must make a payment by the SCOPay app, as we are a cashless school.
Payments are required for all days booked even if the child does not attend, the exceptions being when school is closed/ the child is ill or cancel at least 2 days in advance. You will not be able to cancel bookings on the day of attendance.
Should the child no longer require a place the parent/carer is to advise the School office at least one week in advance, otherwise the parent/carer is still liable for charges. Should the parent/carer fall into arrears, the club will withdraw the child’s place.
To avoid disappointment, please book in advance as places are limited
Activities
The Breakfast Club offers a tasty and healthy breakfast, the most important meal of the day! Choices include:
The Breakfast Club also provides a variety of free play and structured play with a broad range of activities and freedom for children to choose their own activities.
Each morning Mr. Cuming, our PE instructor, takes a selection of children onto the back playground for a range of sports.
A variety of Yoghurts
A variety of Fruits
What the Children Think of Breakfast Club
We really care what the children think about the Breakfast Club and asked them to complete a survey in November 2024. We are delighted to say that our children are having a great time.
Here are some of the things they have said about the club:
"I like the food and seeing my friends"
"It's great, perfect and amazing"
"I think breakfast club is a good and safe environment for kids who arrive early"
"I like the breakfast and playing outside"

Educational Visits
Educational visits are a vital part of life at Our Lady and St Joseph Catholic Primary School. Situated in the heart of London's East End, we are fortunate to have a wealth of cultural, historical, artistic and educational opportunities right on our doorstep. We carefully plan visits that enrich and enhance the curriculum, bringing learning to life and providing memorable experiences for our pupils. Whether exploring local history, visiting museums and galleries, attending theatre performances or engaging with our local community, our trips help children deepen their understanding of the world around them.
As a special celebration of their journey through primary school, our Year 6 pupils take part in a residential visit. This experience provides opportunities for adventure, teamwork, independence and personal growth, while creating lasting memories with friends and staff before they move on to secondary school.

Reading - Understanding Phonics
What is Phonics?
Phonics is a process of breaking words into letters, or groups of letters. Making the sounds of those letters, and putting those sounds together. This then means children can read words starting with sat, tap and pin. Then as they develop into words like snake, or failure.
This may be different to the way you were taught to read, but having a basic understanding can really support your child. It can seem quite daunting and unnatural. Don’t worry. It will seem strange if you have never seen it before, but these videos and pieces of information is aimed to offer you the support needed to help your child.
If you still find it tricky, don’t let it put you off supporting your child. If you can’t grasp it read with your child, give them take up time when they can’t read a word (count to ten in your head), then give them the word. This is much, much better than not reading with your child.
It is also important to note that not all words are decodable. Some words are tricky, like the cannot be taught through phonics the children learn these, and read them at a glance. Some words do not follow phonic patterns like alchemist, these words often follow other spelling patterns and are taught later in school. However most words are phonically decodable. We also offer the children phonically decoable books to ensure they can practise their skills regularly.
KS1 Phonics Screening Check Parent Meeting
Glossary of key terms
Here is a list of the key terms linked to phonics:
Split digraph (previously called magic e): two letters, which work as a pair to make one sound, but are separated within the word e.g. a-e, e-e, i-e, o-e, u-e. For example cake or pine.

Religious Education is taught through the Westminster Scheme of Work and the Diocesan support materials, with Westminster Diocese's guidance. Our Immersion Days provide children with opportunities to explore their topic through a wide range of activities that encourage curiosity, collaboration, creativity and critical thinking. These experiences help children develop a deeper understanding of key historical and geographical concepts whilst building important skills across the wider curriculum.
Rather than teaching History and Geography as isolated weekly lessons, topics are carefully woven throughout other curriculum areas so that learning feels purposeful, connected and meaningful.

Music
"Let your light shine before others, that they may see your good deeds and glorify your Father in heaven." (Matthew 5:16)
Music is an integral part of life at Our Lady & St Joseph's Catholic Primary School and plays an important role in enriching children's spiritual, cultural and creative development. Children participate in weekly music lessons delivered by a specialist music teacher from the Tower Hamlets Arts and Music Education Service (THAMES). Through these lessons, pupils develop their understanding of the National Curriculum for Music through performing, composing, listening and appraising across a range of musical genres and traditions. Where appropriate, learning is meaningfully linked to the wider curriculum, enabling children to make connections between music and their learning in other subject areas.
We are committed to ensuring that music is accessible to all learners. Adaptive teaching is at the heart of our music provision, with lessons carefully planned to meet the needs of all pupils and enable every child to participate, succeed and develop confidence as musicians.
Music is celebrated throughout the school day and is central to our Catholic ethos. Children regularly sing during hymn practices, assemblies and Mass, helping them to develop confidence, performance skills and a love of music. Throughout the year, pupils have opportunities to perform for a variety of audiences through liturgical celebrations, assemblies and school performances.
We work closely with THAMES to enrich our music provision and ensure that children benefit from wider musical experiences beyond the classroom. The school regularly promotes and participates in THAMES projects and opportunities, including collaborative initiatives such as Water Songs: From Bangladesh to the Thames, enabling children to work alongside professional musicians and engage with music within meaningful cultural and community contexts.
To provide as many children as possible with the opportunity to learn an instrument, children in Years 4 to 6 can access group guitar tuition. Delivering lessons in a group setting allows more pupils to develop instrumental skills, musical confidence and enjoyment while learning collaboratively with their peers.
Our school choir rehearses regularly and provides children with a wide range of performance opportunities throughout the year. Choir members proudly represent the school within the local community, performing at venues and events including Tower Hamlets Town Hall, The Seamen's Mission, Canary Wharf and our local residential care home Aspen Court. These experiences allow children to share their talents, bring joy to others and develop confidence, responsibility and a strong sense of community.
Through our partnership with THAMES and our commitment to high-quality music education, we aim to inspire a lifelong appreciation of music and provide memorable musical experiences for all children.

After School Care
Our Lady & St Joseph Catholic Primary School provides After School Care provision for up to 72 children (Y1 – Y6) and up to 32 children (EYFS). This service is invaluable to our school community.
Collection Procedure
After School Care starts at 3:30pm and finishes at 6:00pm.
When you are ready to collect your child, please call 07547447445 (Y1 – Y6) and 07547442239 (EYFS), and a member of staff will bring them to the main gate for you to sign out and collect them.
If you have children in both EYFS & Y1 – Y6 clubs, please call either number and ask for all children you are collecting.
Payment Terms
After School Care costs £7.50 per session. We recommend that payment is made a minimum of 2 days in advance and a credit balance is maintained at all times.
You must make a payment by the SCOPay app, as we are a cashless school.
Payments are required for all days booked even if the child does not attend, the exceptions being when school is closed/ the child is ill or cancel at least 2 days in advance. You will not be able to cancel bookings on the day of attendance.
Should the child no longer require a place the parent/carer is to advise the School office at least one week in advance, otherwise the parent/carer is still liable for charges. Should the parent/carer fall into arrears, the club will withdraw the child’s place.
Activities
During After School Care our children have the opportunity to read, complete their homework, play games and enjoy various sporting activities, supported by a team of high quality trained staff.
Each child attending After School Care receives a healthy snack. This helps them to boost their energy levels and keep them full until they get home for dinner.
a selection of fruits and crudite
Behaviour
All children in After School Care are expected to continue following all school rules until they have been collected by a parent/carer.
A red card system will be in place as a deterrent to inappropriate behaviour. A red card will be given to a child who has been using foul/abusive language, spitting, verbally or physical aggressive to another child or member of staff, leaving supervised areas without permission or exhibiting behaviour that poses a risk to the safety or injury of themselves or another child or member of staff, for example, climbing on tables. If your child is given a red card, an accompanying letter/email will also be given explaining the reason for the red card being given.
If a child collects 3 red cards they will be given a suspension from attending After School Care. The length of the suspension is at the After School Care manager’s discretion and will be dependent on the severity of the behaviour displayed.
If a child's behaviour is deemed to be excessive and a severe breach of the school’s rules and behaviour policy then the school has the right to issue a suspension before the third red card has been given. Children who are actively seen following the school rules and being a shining example of the school’s Gospel Values will be awarded Gospel Value certificates by the After School Care manager.

Passports
Staff are often asked to sign applications for passports/UK residency on behalf of children & parents. This has become increasingly time consuming and may later involve resolving queries with the passport office.
Unfortunately, a decision has been made to withdraw this service. Please do not approach staff with requests as they also have the right to safeguard their own sensitive data.
